text:
lina: FYI customer hitting intermittent 401s and import errors after they upgraded our python SDK in their CI. can someone triage? :eyes:

alec: brief summary from customer: poetry managed env, CI runs tests in a docker image with --system-site-packages, after upgrading redwood sdk they see ImportError: cannot import name 'TokenAuth' from 'redwood' and auth starts failing intermittently (some requests 401).
maria: ugh that --system-site-packages flag often surfaces duplicates. ask for `pip show redwood-sdk` vs `poetry show redwood-sdk` output.
lina: asked for repro steps and they pasted this snippet:```dockerfile
FROM python:3.10-slim
RUN pip install poetry
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml poetry.lock ./
RUN poetry install --no-interaction --no-ansi
COPY . .
RUN pytest
```
plus CI sets ENV: `PYTHONPATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages` (they later admitted).
alec: logs they sent:```Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/tests/test_client.py", line 12, in <module>
    from redwood import Client
ImportError: cannot import name 'TokenAuth' from 'redwood' (/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py)```
maria: that path points to system site-packages. likely an old wheel/pip-installed package shadowing the poetry virtualenv package. That would explain intermittent 401s if CI intermittently picks the wrong install (system vs venv).
lina: customer also said they had a local dev editable install previously: `pip install -e .` in dev env, maybe left behind metadata. asked them to run these repro commands and paste back: ``pip list | grep redwood && python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)" && poetry run python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)"``
support-bot: step created: gather package paths, check for duplicate installs.
alec: suggested immediate workaround: uninstall system copy before poetry install: `pip uninstall redwood-sdk -y` or ensure Docker build does not use --system-site-packages. also recommend pinning the package name they import vs distribution name confusion: our package on PyPI is `redwood-sdk` but import is `redwood` — duplicates happen.
maria: posted minimal repro they used locally:```
# reproduce (on host)
pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.4
python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)"
poetry new repro && cd repro
# add redwood-sdk (different version) to pyproject, poetry install
poetry add redwood-sdk@0.10.0
poetry run python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)"
```
lina: customer ran pip list and showed two entries: one in /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages (0.9.4) and their venv had 0.10.0. they uninstalled system copy and CI greened up.
alec: long-term suggestions for them: 1) avoid system site-packages in CI, 2) use `python -m pip` consistently inside the same interpreter, 3) prefer `poetry export -f requirements.txt --dev` + `pip install -r` in Docker for deterministic installs, 4) run `python -c "import importlib, pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.iter_modules())[:10])"` if weird.
maria: also flagged packaging issue we should document: precedence of distribution names vs import path. opened a quick internal note to add a troubleshooting entry in docs: "duplicate installs / system-site-packages causing ImportError and auth 401s".
lina: customer asked if we can change the package name to avoid confusion. we replied: not feasible short-term. suggested we add clearer messaging in SDK error when TokenAuth missing (fallback detection).
alec: low-effort SDK improvement idea: at import time check for version mismatch between installed distribution metadata and expected api surface and warn in stderr when running in CI. filed ticket INF-739.
maria: final from customer: uninstalled system package, removed PYTHONPATH, CI no longer sees ImportError, 401s stopped. closing for now. :white_check_mark:
